namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae722978db.summary: Converts the CSR to a dense host adjacency matrix and invokes the CUDA-MS clique search. The returned bitmasks are copied into GraphMine-owned result values.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae722978db.returns: A MaximumCliqueBackendResult containing status, one clique as dense vertex indices, the size of the optional upper mask, and search-plus-synchronization time in milliseconds. An absent upper mask produces an upper-size field of zero.
details: An empty graph succeeds before any device check. Nonempty inputs require a signed 32-bit vertex count; negative device ordinals are invalid_argument, and unavailable devices are backend_unavailable.
The adapter stores an n-by-n byte matrix. Matrix-size overflow or caught matrix allocation failure returns resource_exhausted.
The upstream call uses fixed search parameters. A negative returned size, null clique mask, or failed synchronization returns execution_failed; both masks are released with mask_free.
This layer decodes the witness but does not itself verify every pair of returned vertices or establish an optimality certificate.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a5ef6d17d1.summary: Counts maximal bicliques with cuMBE after building adjacency in both directions and placing the smaller partition on the candidate side.

parameters.input: Borrowed left-to-right bipartite CSR. Partition counts and edge indices must fit signed 32-bit integers; neighbors are right-partition indices, not global graph IDs.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a5ef6d17d1.returns: A MaximalBicliqueBackendResult with status, the count, and enumeration-kernel time in milliseconds. No biclique vertex sets are materialized by this adapter.
details: An empty partition or empty edge array returns a successful zero count before preparation or device access.
prepare_graph checks offsets, row bounds, and neighbor bounds. Invalid preparation and caught CUDA exceptions become execution_failed; oversized partition counts return unsupported.
The device must support cooperative kernel launches and at least 512 threads per block. Workspace block count is limited by cooperative occupancy.
ManagedArena owns the CUDA managed allocations for graph data and search workspace until the call completes. Calls are serialized because the upstream kernels share state.
Workspace size overflow and a negative signed 32-bit result counter return resource_exhausted. The negative-counter check is not a general proof against all possible counter wraparound.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae82e1ede3.summary: Provides the cuQC adapter boundary when no executable cuQC backend is linked. The current implementation always reports that the backend is unavailable.

parameters.graph: Graph argument reserved by the backend interface; the stub does not read it.
parameters.minimum_degree_ratio: Requested minimum-degree ratio reserved by the interface; unused by the stub.
parameters.minimum_size: Requested minimum quasi-clique size reserved by the interface; unused by the stub.
parameters.static_scheduling: Requested static-scheduling flag reserved by the interface; unused by the stub.
parameters.device_id: Requested CUDA device ordinal; the stub does not query or select a device.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae82e1ede3.returns: QuasiCliqueBackendResult with backend_unavailable, an empty quasi_cliques vector, and elapsed_ms equal to zero.
details: No parameter validation or computation occurs, including for empty graphs. This function does not implement a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a06e9330cf.summary: Runs the DuMato induced-motif engine and sums per-warp canonical-graph counters into GraphMine's common motif ordering.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.motif_size: Motif vertex count; only 3 and 4 are accepted by this adapter.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a06e9330cf.returns: GraphMotifBackendResult with status, two or six owned uint64 counts, and elapsed milliseconds covering engine setup, search, result transfer, and aggregation.
details: Counts use the common order: size 3 = triangle, path of length two; size 4 = three-star, four-vertex path, tailed triangle, four-cycle, diamond, four-clique.
Graphs with fewer vertices than the motif size or no adjacency entries return an all-zero count vector before device access. Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit signed 32-bit integers.
The adapter converts offsets to signed 64-bit and neighbors to signed 32-bit storage, serializes the upstream engine, and copies per-warp hashes from device memory before aggregation.

Unsupported sizes and index widths return unsupported; unusable devices return backend_unavailable; result transfer errors return execution_failed; an unexpected canonical vector shape returns internal_error.
Caught host allocation failure returns resource_exhausted. Other caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a1c115aff5.summary: Runs EDTC on a batch of edge deletions and insertions and returns their separate triangle-count changes.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.updates: Borrowed, already validated dense-endpoint edge updates. insertion selects addition versus deletion; endpoints and update consistency must be checked by the caller.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a1c115aff5.returns: DynamicTriangleBackendResult with status, triangles deleted, triangles inserted, and elapsed call time in milliseconds. The input CSR is not changed and no updated CSR is returned.
details: An empty batch succeeds with zero deltas before device access. Vertex, adjacency-entry, and update counts must each be at most UINT_MAX - 2 to leave room for sentinels.
Two temporary isolated vertices and their edge supply a deletion/reinsertion pair. They add no triangles while preserving the upstream pipeline's requirement for both update kinds.
The adapter passes deletion and insertion records to the upstream batch routine; semantic validation and canonical batch preparation belong to the public facade.
Device discovery failure returns backend_unavailable; a pending CUDA error after execution or a caught exception returns execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1af1f171581.summary: Prepares device-specific launch dimensions and invokes the Everest temporal feed-forward motif kernel through the common CUDA runner.

parameters.input: Borrowed, validated temporal input with dense signed 32-bit endpoints, events sorted by timestamp, and nonnegative relative timestamps and window. Event count, vertex count, and timestamp plus window must fit signed 32-bit values; normalization belongs to the public facade.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1af1f171581.returns: TemporalMotifBackendResult with status, the motif count, and elapsed runner time in milliseconds. It returns a count only, not event triples.
details: An empty event array succeeds before device access. Input format and range checks belong to the public temporal-motif facade.
The supported pattern is A to B, then B to C, then A to C on distinct vertices with strictly increasing event times and final-minus-first time no greater than max_time_span.
Dispatch and expansion grid sizes are each derived from kernel occupancy using 96 threads per block. The common runner owns all temporary CUDA buffers.
Device discovery failure returns backend_unavailable. Device setup, occupancy, allocation, execution, and synchronization exceptions become execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a9329da32a.summary: Copies the canonical CSR into the GraphMiner graph representation and invokes its induced-motif counter for three or four vertices.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.motif_size: Motif vertex count; only 3 and 4 are supported.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a9329da32a.returns: GraphMotifBackendResult with status, two or six owned uint64 counts, and solver-plus-synchronization time in milliseconds.
details: Counts use the common order: size 3 = triangle, path of length two; size 4 = three-star, four-vertex path, tailed triangle, four-cycle, diamond, four-clique.
A graph with fewer vertices than the requested motif size returns a zero vector before device access. Vertex counts must fit signed 32-bit integers and adjacency counts signed 64-bit integers.
The solver receives the fixed adapter configuration 1 and 1024 for its final two arguments. Execution is serialized, followed by CUDA synchronization.
Unsupported size or index width returns unsupported; device selection failure returns backend_unavailable; synchronization failures and caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0210a9668.summary: Counts k-cliques with GAMMA by expanding ordered embeddings from vertices whose degree is at least k - 1.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.k: Requested clique size; the compiled adapter accepts 3 through 7.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0210a9668.returns: KCliqueBackendResult with status, a uint64 count, and expansion time in milliseconds. The adapter returns a count only, with no clique witnesses.
details: Fewer than k vertices or no degree-eligible roots yields a successful zero count before device access. Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit unsigned 32-bit integers.
CSR offsets and access flags use device allocations; adjacency uses managed memory with a read-mostly hint. Root storage is released after initializing the first embedding level.
For each level, the expansion constraint requires adjacency to all prior vertices and their ordering, preventing permutation duplicates.
Calls are serialized. The cleanup helper attempts to release graph, embeddings, and access-controller storage on both normal completion and caught exceptions.
Unsupported k or sizes return unsupported; unusable devices return backend_unavailable; caught execution exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a6d335ab2d.summary: Builds an unweighted gLeiden graph from incident vertices, computes communities, and maps the labels back to the original dense vertex order.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a6d335ab2d.returns: CommunityDetectionBackendResult with status, one owned label per vertex, and elapsed GPU call time. native_modularity is absent for nontrivial executions and is zero for empty or all-isolate graphs.
details: Isolated vertices bypass the upstream refinement kernel and receive separate singleton labels. An empty graph or a graph containing only isolates succeeds without a device query.
Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit signed 32-bit integers. Both adjacency directions are filled with unit edge weights.
Calls are serialized because the upstream original-to-current mapping is shared. Negative output labels return correctness_mismatch.
Unavailable devices return backend_unavailable. Device selection or pending CUDA errors use execution_failed; caught exceptions also return execution_failed.
The adapter supplies no resolution argument and does not claim that the heuristic partition is a globally optimal modularity partition.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ace868cb30.summary: Counts label-preserving subgraph embeddings with gMatch after reordering the query and constructing candidate sets on the GPU.

parameters.data_graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.data_labels: One integer label per data vertex, in dense vertex order; borrowed for this call.
parameters.query_graph: Borrowed simple undirected query CSR. Its labels and structure must meet the public gMatch support checks before this internal adapter is called.
parameters.query_labels: One integer label per query vertex; label codes must use the same equality convention as data_labels.
parameters.initial_match_capacity: Initial match-buffer capacity passed to the join routine; must be a positive value no larger than INT_MAX for nontrivial queries.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ace868cb30.returns: SubgraphIsomorphismBackendResult with status, the embedding count including restored query symmetries, and milliseconds covering candidate construction and joining. It does not return mappings.
details: The empty query has one embedding. A query larger than the data has none. A one-vertex query counts matching labels directly, before device access or capacity validation.
The public facade restricts the validated path to at most 16 query vertices and 32767 data vertices; this adapter relies on those checks and does not repeat them or label-length validation.
For a symmetry factor of one, the ordinary BFS/DFS join is used. Otherwise the symmetry-reduced join count is multiplied by the query's factor.
Calls are serialized. GPU query, data, and candidate allocations are explicitly deallocated on the successful path after synchronization; caught exceptions become execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0eee63b08.summary: Invokes GPUMaximumClique on in-memory CSR and copies one maximum-clique witness, optionally retaining every returned tie.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.
parameters.known_lower_bound: Caller-supplied lower-bound size. This adapter intentionally does not use it for pruning because no witness accompanies it; the public facade checks it.
parameters.return_all_ties: When true, request all tied maximum cliques from the upstream implementation and copy them into tied_cliques.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0eee63b08.returns: MaximumCliqueBackendResult with status, the first returned clique, its size in relaxation_upper_size, upstream elapsed time, and optional tied_cliques. All returned vertex vectors own their storage.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device access. Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit unsigned 32-bit integers.
Execution is serialized and uses the validated breadth-first configuration with one run and windowing disabled.
CUDA failure or a completed search with no clique returns execution_failed. An upstream out-of-memory flag returns resource_exhausted rather than presenting a partial search as complete.
The adapter copies vertex results but leaves common witness and lower-bound validation to the public facade.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0c9941f1d.summary: Orients each undirected edge by degree and vertex ID, then counts k-cliques with the GraphSet kernel.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.k: Requested clique size; only 3 through 6 are supported by this validated kernel.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0c9941f1d.returns: KCliqueBackendResult with status, the clique count, and kernel-plus-synchronization time in milliseconds. No clique sets are returned.
details: Fewer than k vertices produces a zero count before device access. Vertex count must fit signed 32-bit integers and the undirected edge count signed 64-bit integers.

Edges point from lower degree to higher degree, breaking equal-degree ties by increasing vertex ID. The adapter rejects an oriented degree above 1280 because the kernel reserves twenty 64-bit partitions.
The oriented host graph owns copies of its arrays. Calls are serialized around the upstream counter.

Input limits return unsupported; unusable devices return backend_unavailable; caught host allocation failure returns resource_exhausted; other exceptions or synchronization failures return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae2c3f3e37.summary: Runs GraphSet's non-induced three- or four-vertex motif counter, using a CPU triangle statistic to prepare the upstream graph.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.motif_size: Motif vertex count; only 3 and 4 are supported.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae2c3f3e37.returns: GraphMotifBackendResult with status, reordered owned counts, and upstream counter-plus-synchronization time in milliseconds. CPU triangle preprocessing is outside that measured interval.
details: Counts use the common order: size 3 = triangle, path of length two; size 4 = three-star, four-vertex path, tailed triangle, four-cycle, diamond, four-clique.

Too few vertices or no adjacency entries returns a zero vector before device access. Vertex count and maximum degree must fit signed 32-bit integers; adjacency count and the triangle statistic must fit signed 64-bit integers.
The adapter sets GraphSet's shared maximum-intersection capacity while holding a mutex and passes owned copies of the CSR arrays to the upstream graph.
Unsupported sizes/statistics return unsupported; device failures return backend_unavailable; unexpected count-vector length returns internal_error.
Caught host allocation failure returns resource_exhausted. Synchronization failures and other caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae9edd2234.summary: Counts k-cliques with KCGPU's validated PIV-8-BE configuration after degree orientation and one-based remapping.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.k: Requested clique size; the adapter accepts 3 through 10.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ae9edd2234.returns: KCliqueBackendResult with status, a uint64 count, and kernel execution time in milliseconds. Clique witnesses are not materialized.
details: Fewer than k vertices returns a successful zero before device access. The adapter checks unsigned 32-bit vertex and undirected-edge counts, then adds an isolated zero sentinel for the upstream layout.
Oriented edges point from lower degree to higher degree, breaking ties by increasing vertex ID. Every oriented degree must be at most 1000.
A host calculation sums choose(oriented_degree, k - 1) bounds and rejects inputs for which it cannot certify that the count fits uint64.
DeviceGraph owns the device CSR/COO arrays. Allocation failure returns resource_exhausted; copy/kernel failures and caught exceptions return execution_failed; unsupported bounds return unsupported.
The adapter serializes the kernel invocation and explicitly releases the algorithm's resources and stream on successful completion.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a2f2f8ec45.summary: Runs KCoreGPU's level-by-level peeling kernels and copies the final core number for every vertex back to host memory.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a2f2f8ec45.returns: KCoreBackendResult with status, an owned vector of core numbers in input vertex order, and peeling-loop time in milliseconds. Transfers and graph preparation are outside the measured loop.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device checks. A negative device ordinal returns invalid_argument; an unavailable device returns backend_unavailable.
BackendGraph converts counts, offsets, and degrees to unsigned 32-bit values. Conversion errors are caught as execution_failed by this wrapper.
At each level the kernels select and process vertices, synchronize, and read the cumulative processed count. The loop ends when all vertices have been processed.
Device adjacency, degree, progress, and work buffers are allocated for the call and explicitly freed along the handled success and CUDA-error paths.
The final degree buffer is interpreted as core numbers. CUDA problem failures and caught exceptions return execution_failed with no result vector.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0492791d4.summary: Counts maximal cliques with the G2-AIMD sequential-expansion application and its GPU pipeline executor.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a0492791d4.returns: BackendCountResult with status, the total maximal-clique count, and executor-plus-synchronization time in milliseconds. The adapter returns no clique vertex sets.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device access. Vertex and edge-array sizes must fit the upstream index types; maximum degree must be strictly below the 100000-entry per-warp temporary capacity.
The requested device must also fit the upstream eight-slot device table. Calls are serialized.
All dense vertices are submitted as sources. The executor receives a 16000000-entry buffer cap and borrowed host CSR copies that remain alive through execution.

Input capacity limits return unsupported; device failures return backend_unavailable; caught execution errors return execution_failed. Public handling of isolated-vertex cliques belongs to the facade.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a66f44c4c0.summary: Builds the mce-gpu one-based CSR/COO layout, orders it by core priority, and runs maximal-clique counting.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a66f44c4c0.returns: BackendCountResult with status, the maximal-clique count, and counter execution time in milliseconds. Graph preparation and core ordering are outside that measured interval.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device access. The vertex count must be at most UINT_MAX - 1 to leave an isolated zero sentinel; adjacency count must fit unsigned 32-bit integers.
Managed graph arrays are copied and split by core priority. The original arrays are freed before counting; the oriented arrays are freed on the successful completion path.
The kernel uses one partition when the computed core bound is at most 300 and eight otherwise. Public handling of genuine isolated vertices belongs to the facade.
Unsupported sizes return unsupported; device selection failures return backend_unavailable; caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a78ebd38ff.summary: Copies the canonical graph into RDMCE, orders vertices by degree, rebuilds its CSR, and invokes the pivot-based maximal-clique solver.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a78ebd38ff.returns: BackendCountResult with status, the returned maximal-clique count, and solver-call time in milliseconds. Host conversion and ordering are outside that measured interval.
details: An empty graph succeeds without CUDA. A negative device ordinal returns invalid_argument; a failed device query or selection returns backend_unavailable.
CanonicalRdmceGraph checks its vertex index range and requires an even number of adjacency entries, but assumes the caller has established full undirected symmetry.
The adapter returns a count only. It relies on the solver for execution and leaves common completeness/witness handling to the public facade.
Exceptions from graph conversion or the solver are translated to execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1aa985ccc64.summary: Runs Maximum-Clique-on-GPU with core reduction, a retained heuristic witness, and exact search on the reduced graph when the bound is not already met.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.
parameters.known_lower_bound: Caller-provided lower-bound size. This adapter ignores it for pruning and seeds search from an actual preprocessing clique; the public facade checks the caller's bound.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1aa985ccc64.returns: MaximumCliqueBackendResult with status, one owned clique in original dense indices, a core-derived upper-size bound, and total adapter execution time in milliseconds. It does not enumerate tied optima.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device access. Vertex count must be at most UINT_MAX - 1 for the zero sentinel, and adjacency count must fit unsigned 32-bit integers.
The preprocessing witness is returned immediately when its size equals maximum core number plus one, or when reduction leaves no candidate vertices.
Otherwise the adapter reduces by the witness size, sorts surviving vertices by core number, applies the same permutation to degrees, and runs the evaluation path that retains clique vertices.

A larger returned clique is mapped through the surviving original-name array and the one-based sentinel offset is removed. Missing preprocessing vertices or invalid reduced vertices cause execution_failed.
DeviceGraphStorage owns original, reduced, and split graph arrays. Calls are serialized; unusable devices return backend_unavailable, and caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a9295d4072.summary: Prepares device-specific launch dimensions and invokes the Mayura temporal feed-forward motif kernel through the common CUDA runner.

parameters.input: Borrowed, validated temporal input with dense signed 32-bit endpoints, events sorted by timestamp, and nonnegative relative timestamps and window. Event count, vertex count, and timestamp plus window must fit signed 32-bit values; normalization belongs to the public facade.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a9295d4072.returns: TemporalMotifBackendResult with status, the motif count, and elapsed runner time in milliseconds. It returns a count only, not event triples.
details: An empty event array succeeds before device access. Input format and range checks belong to the public temporal-motif facade.
The supported pattern is A to B, then B to C, then A to C on distinct vertices with strictly increasing event times and final-minus-first time no greater than max_time_span.
Dispatch and expansion grid sizes are each derived from kernel occupancy using 96 threads per block. The common runner owns all temporary CUDA buffers.
Device discovery failure returns backend_unavailable. Device setup, occupancy, allocation, execution, and synchronization exceptions become execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a830ced3a7.summary: Runs a selected parallel Louvain or Leiden variant on a Kokkos graph with unit edge weights and degree-based vertex weights.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.
parameters.algorithm: One of parallel_louvain, parallel_leiden, or parallel_leiden_plus. The switch has no fallback for an invalid enum value.
parameters.resolution: Modularity resolution passed to the objective; the public facade must validate that it is finite and nonnegative. This adapter does not repeat that check.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a830ced3a7.returns: CommunityDetectionBackendResult with status, an owned label per vertex, the upstream modularity objective, and elapsed milliseconds covering matrix construction, clustering, and result transfer.
details: An empty graph succeeds with empty labels and modularity zero before device access. Vertex and adjacency counts must fit the compiled Kokkos index types, described by this adapter as signed 32-bit.
Calls are serialized. Kokkos is initialized once if needed and cannot be switched to another device by this adapter after initialization.
The modularity objective is refreshed after setting resolution, before convergence decisions and state copies.
The adapter fences the computation, copies labels to host, and rejects negative or out-of-range labels with correctness_mismatch. It does not promise globally optimal communities.
Unavailable devices return backend_unavailable; unsupported index ranges return unsupported; initialization conflicts and other caught exceptions return execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ace30ca592.summary: Builds a unit-weight device COO matrix, converts it to ToT's bitmap representation, and counts triangles through tensor problems.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ace30ca592.returns: TriangleBackendResult with status, the undirected triangle count, and bitmap-conversion-plus-kernel time in milliseconds.
details: Fewer than three vertices or fewer than three undirected edges returns zero without device access. Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit signed 32-bit integers.

The tensor routine counts directed closed walks on symmetric adjacency. The adapter requires divisibility by six and divides by six to obtain undirected triangles; a remainder produces correctness_mismatch.

Thrust and ToT containers manage temporary matrix storage. Unsupported sizes return unsupported, unusable devices backend_unavailable, and synchronization failures or caught exceptions execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ad16b60cbb.summary: Runs TurboBC from every vertex and converts the returned float betweenness scores to an owned double vector.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1ad16b60cbb.returns: BetweennessCentralityBackendResult with status, one raw score per dense vertex, and upstream call time in milliseconds. Widening floats to double does not recover precision lost in the GPU computation.
details: An empty graph succeeds before device access. Vertex count, adjacency count, and every CSR offset must fit signed 32-bit integers.
The adapter allocates host levels, path-count, and score arrays and calls the external routine with all vertices as sources, first source zero, and one repetition.
Scores are not rescaled here; the public facade applies its documented centrality conventions and checks.
Calls are serialized. A failed device selection, a nonzero external return code, a pending CUDA error, or a caught exception returns execution_failed. Index-width limits return unsupported.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a167ad2dfe.summary: Uses WeTriC's CPU degree-ordering preprocessing and CUDA triangle counter on an in-memory canonical graph.

parameters.graph: Borrowed simple, symmetric, undirected CSR in dense zero-based vertex order. Offsets and neighbor indices must be valid and rows sorted; this adapter does not validate the entire CSR contract.
parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal to select for this call; the enabled backend must be able to use that device. The input graph remains owned by the caller.
parameters.spread: Positive WeTriC spread tuning parameter. Its shared-memory requirement is (2 * 128 * spread + 1) uint32 values and must fit the selected device's per-block limit.
parameters.adjacency_matrix_length: Positive WeTriC adjacency-matrix length, required to be a multiple of 64.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1a167ad2dfe.returns: TriangleBackendResult with status, the triangle count, and GPU counter call time in milliseconds. CPU preprocessing and graph release are outside that measured interval.
details: Fewer than three vertices or fewer than three undirected edges returns zero before parameter or device checks. Vertex and adjacency-entry counts must fit unsigned 32-bit integers.
Invalid tuning values return invalid_argument. Oversized indices or shared-memory requirements return unsupported, and unusable devices return backend_unavailable.
The CPU preprocessing result is released after a successful counter call. The upstream exit hook throws WetricUpstreamError so an abort becomes execution_failed instead of terminating the process.
A pending CUDA error or any caught standard exception returns execution_failed.
When this backend is disabled at build time, the linked stub returns backend_unavailable immediately, with empty or zero result fields and zero elapsed time; it does not attempt a CPU fallback.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Converts a failed CUDA runtime result into a C++ exception with the problem name and CUDA error description.

details: The enclosing adapter catches standard exceptions and translates them to an execution_failed Status.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymous__n.summary: Constructs an empty owner for cuMBE CUDA managed-memory allocations.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymous__n.returns: No object can be created through this overload; attempting to use it is a compile-time error.

Successful nonzero allocations are retained until the arena is destroyed; no per-allocation release API is provided.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Validates bipartite CSR boundaries, builds reverse adjacency, and chooses the smaller partition as cuMBE's candidate side.

parameters.input: Borrowed left-to-right bipartite CSR. Partition counts must already fit int; right_neighbors contains partition-local right vertex indices.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: An owned HostBipartiteGraph with signed-int node ranges and edge arrays in both directions. num_r is the smaller side; equal sizes place the original left side there.

Rejects an edge-array length above INT_MAX or any right neighbor outside its partition with std::invalid_argument.
The transpose is filled by scanning left vertices in increasing order. Duplicate edges are not removed and rows are not generally sorted by this helper.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Assigns the same value to a contiguous host-accessible range, including cuMBE managed-memory work arrays.

parameters.count: Number of consecutive elements to fill.
parameters.value: Value copied into every destination element.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: The range [destination, destination + count) is overwritten through std::fill; ownership is unchanged.
details: The destination must be accessible to the CPU. This is not a CUDA kernel launch or a device-only-memory fill.

dumato__motif_8cu_1a3ae1e6fd0dfa0cdd51fd.summary: Declares the upstream CUDA motif kernel selected by the DuMato adapter. Its kernel body is supplied by the linked DuMato artifact.

parameters.$5: Unnamed upstream configuration argument; the first-party adapter passes 1024.

structgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymous__.returns: The graph's recorded pointers are passed to cudaFree in that order. Free errors are ignored and any borrowed pointer into these allocations is invalid afterward.
details: The caller must finish work that uses these graph arrays before destroying the owner.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Copies an upstream clique array to host and translates one-based vertex names back to GraphMine's zero-based indices.

parameters.values: Borrowed upstream GPUArray whose first count elements contain original one-based vertex names.
parameters.count: Number of values requested; zero or a count above values.N returns an empty vector.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: An owned vector in input order with sentinel zeros omitted and every other value decremented by one. The vector can therefore contain fewer than count entries.
details: The temporary CPU array returned by copytocpu is released with std::free after conversion. The source GPUArray remains owned by the caller.
This helper does not sort vertices, remove repeated nonzero names, or verify clique adjacency.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Returns the process-lifetime bookkeeping record for the Kokkos runtime used by the clustering adapter.
namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: A reference to one lazily allocated KokkosRuntime containing ownership, finalizer-registration, and selected-device state.
details: The record is intentionally not destroyed during static teardown. ensure_kokkos registers a separate exit handler after initialization so Kokkos can finalize in the required order.
This function does not itself initialize or finalize Kokkos. Calls that change the state are serialized by the surrounding clustering adapter.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Initializes Kokkos for the requested CUDA device when needed, or verifies that an existing runtime is compatible with that request.

parameters.device_id: CUDA device ordinal expected by the caller. If Kokkos is already initialized, it must match the recorded or discovered active device.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: On normal return, Kokkos is initialized and no known device conflict exists. Throws std::invalid_argument if an existing runtime belongs to another device.
details: When this adapter initializes Kokkos, it marks ownership and registers one exit handler that finalizes only while Kokkos is still initialized.
For an externally initialized runtime with unknown recorded device, it tries cudaGetDevice; it does not take ownership or register finalization.
Initialization exceptions propagate to run_pggc. A failed device-discovery query for an existing runtime leaves the device unknown rather than proving compatibility.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Copies CSR topology to Kokkos device views and constructs the unweighted matrix representation used by parallel clustering.

parameters.graph: Borrowed canonical CSR with counts and indices already validated for ordinal_t and edge_offset_t. Kokkos must be initialized before calling.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: A matrix_t retaining the device neighbor and offset views. Its explicit edge-weight view is empty; the clustering caller marks the graph as having uniform edges.
details: Host mirror views are filled and deep-copied to device storage. The returned matrix does not borrow the input graph's vectors.
This helper casts sizes and indices without independent range validation.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Builds a Kokkos device vector whose entry for each vertex is its CSR degree.

parameters.graph: Borrowed CSR with valid offsets and index ranges already checked by the caller; Kokkos must be initialized.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: A PggcWeightView owning a device allocation of graph.vertex_count() values, filled with offsets[v + 1] - offsets[v] converted to value_t.
details: The helper computes degrees in a host mirror and deep-copies them to the device. It does not read stored edge weights.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal.summary: Converts a failed CUDA runtime result into a C++ exception with the problem name and CUDA error description.

parameters.code: CUDA status code returned by the problem being checked.
parameters.problem: Description of the failed problem; a C-string argument must be non-null.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal.returns: Returns normally for cudaSuccess; otherwise throws std::runtime_error. It does not clear CUDA error state or release resources.
details: The enclosing adapter catches standard exceptions and translates them to an execution_failed Status.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Constructs an empty noncopyable owner for a temporal-kernel CUDA buffer.
classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: An object with a null device pointer and zero element count. No allocation or initialization occurs.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Constructs a temporal-kernel buffer and allocates device storage for count elements.

parameters.count: Number of T elements; count * sizeof(T) must fit std::size_t. Zero leaves the buffer empty.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: A buffer owning uninitialized CUDA device storage, released by its destructor. Allocation failure throws std::runtime_error.
details: The constructor delegates to allocate. It does not initialize element values; call zero or copy_from before a kernel reads them.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Disables copy construction of a CUDA buffer owner so its device allocation has a single cleanup owner.

parameters.$1: Source buffer; this overload is deleted.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: No buffer can be created through this overload; using it is a compile-time error.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Disables copy assignment of a temporal CUDA buffer owner.

parameters.$1: Source buffer; this overload is deleted.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: No device pointer or ownership is copied; using this overload is a compile-time error.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Frees the temporal-kernel device allocation if this buffer owns one.
classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: Passes the stored pointer to cudaFree and ignores the return code. All pointers obtained with get() become invalid.
details: The surrounding runner synchronizes its work before normal scope exit. Buffer destruction is also used during exception unwinding.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Allocates uninitialized CUDA storage and records the requested element count.

parameters.count: Number of T elements. This helper is intended for an empty buffer, and count * sizeof(T) must fit std::size_t.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: For nonzero count, installs the newly allocated device pointer and size. Zero leaves the current pointer and size unchanged.
details: A failed cudaMalloc throws std::runtime_error. The byte multiplication is not overflow-checked.
The method does not free an existing allocation before overwriting its pointer; call it only on an unallocated buffer.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Clears every byte of the owned device allocation to zero.
classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: The allocated range is zero-filled with cudaMemset; an empty buffer is unchanged. CUDA failure throws std::runtime_error.
details: This applies byte-zero initialization, so callers must use types whose intended zero state is represented by all-zero bytes.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Copies an entire host vector into an already allocated CUDA buffer with the same element count.

parameters.source: Borrowed host vector to copy. Its size must exactly match this buffer's recorded count.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: The device range contains a byte copy of source. Empty matching vectors require no CUDA copy; ownership of both allocations stays unchanged.
details: A size mismatch throws std::logic_error before copying. A failed cudaMemcpy throws std::runtime_error.
The problem uses cudaMemcpyHostToDevice and does not resize or allocate the buffer. T must be suitable for this raw-memory copy.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Exposes the temporal buffer's device address without transferring allocation ownership.
classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: A borrowed mutable T* into the owned CUDA allocation, or nullptr for an empty buffer. It is valid only while the owner retains the allocation.
details: The returned address is for CUDA work or CUDA copy problems; it is not a host copy and must not be freed by the caller.

classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.summary: Exposes the temporal buffer's device address without transferring allocation ownership.
classgraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal__cu.returns: A borrowed const T* into the owned CUDA allocation, or nullptr for an empty buffer. It is valid only while the owner retains the allocation.
details: The returned address is for CUDA work or CUDA copy problems; it is not a host copy and must not be freed by the caller.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal.summary: Builds temporal event indexes and the fixed feed-forward motif, owns the CUDA workspace, and calls a backend-specific runner.

parameters.input: Borrowed, validated temporal input with dense signed 32-bit endpoints, events sorted by timestamp, and nonnegative relative timestamps and window. Event count, vertex count, and timestamp plus window must fit signed 32-bit values; normalization belongs to the public facade.
parameters.device_id: Device ordinal carried through the adapter interface. This helper does not read it or select a device; the caller must already have selected the correct CUDA context.
parameters.dispatch_blocks: Dispatch-kernel grid size recorded in the Invocation passed to runner.
parameters.expansion_blocks: Expansion-kernel grid size recorded in the Invocation passed to runner.
parameters.block_size: Threads per block recorded in the Invocation; the current backend callers use 96.
parameters.backend_name: Non-null backend label used in synchronization and failure messages.
parameters.runner: Callable accepting the prepared Invocation and returning the motif count. It borrows all invocation pointers and must not retain them beyond this call.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1temporal.returns: TemporalMotifBackendResult with success, the runner's count converted to uint64, and total setup/execute/synchronization time. Caught standard exceptions produce execution_failed, zero count, and zero time.
details: Host event indexes group incoming and outgoing event indices by dense vertex while retaining event order within each group.
The fixed motif descriptors extend A to B with B to C and then constrain A to C. The invocation uses three motif edges and input.max_time_span as its time window.
Every event/index/descriptor array and work buffer is owned by a local DeviceBuffer. Offload storage has 2092 * 96 Context entries; counters and control buffers start at zero.
The helper synchronizes CUDA after runner returns, then its buffers are released on scope exit. Endpoint bounds, temporal ordering, index widths, and launch dimensions are caller preconditions.

turbobc_8cu_1a0e4154d65b41ca334b749ef3b1.summary: Declares the C-linkage TurboBC entry point called with host CSR arrays and host scratch/output vectors.

parameters.row_indices: Borrowed host neighbor-index array of length nonzeros; the adapter passes its CSR neighbors through this upstream argument name.
parameters.column_offsets: Borrowed host CSR offset array of length vertex_count + 1, represented as signed int.
parameters.levels: Writable host traversal-level buffer of vertex_count integers, initialized to zero by the adapter.
parameters.path_counts: Writable host path-count buffer of vertex_count floats, initialized to zero by the adapter.
parameters.scores: Writable host output-score buffer of vertex_count floats, initialized to zero by the adapter.
parameters.source_count: Number of source vertices requested; GraphMine passes vertex_count to process every source.
parameters.first_source: First requested source index; GraphMine passes zero.
parameters.nonzeros: Number of adjacency entries in row_indices.
parameters.vertex_count: Number of dense graph vertices and entries in each per-vertex buffer.
parameters.repetition_count: Upstream repetition count; GraphMine passes one.

turbobc_8cu_1a0e4154d65b41ca334b749ef3b1.returns: An integer result code interpreted by run_turbobc as success when zero and failure otherwise. Scores are delivered through scores.
details: This adapter contains only the declaration. CUDA allocation details and traversal implementation belong to the linked TurboBC artifact.
GraphMine keeps all supplied arrays alive throughout the call, then checks the return code and CUDA error state before exposing a result.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.summary: Wraps a CUDA runtime result in the GraphMine Status type and adds the problem context on failure.

parameters.problem: Non-null problem description included in an error message.

namespacegraphmine_1_1detail_1_1anonymou.returns: Status::success() for cudaSuccess; otherwise execution_failed with the problem and CUDA error text.
details: This helper does not throw intentionally, synchronize work, or query a new CUDA error; it describes the supplied code.

classanonymous__namespace_02wetric_8cu_0.summary: Constructs the exception used to turn a WeTriC upstream abort into a recoverable adapter error.

parameters.code: Exit code supplied by the upstream routine; it is included in the exception message.

classanonymous__namespace_02wetric_8cu_0.returns: A std::runtime_error-derived object with a message identifying the WeTriC abort code. Construction alone does not throw this object.

namespaceanonymous__namespace_02wetric_8.summary: Replaces the upstream WeTriC exit call with an exception so the library caller can receive a Status failure.

parameters.code: Exit code requested by the upstream code, preserved in the exception message.

namespaceanonymous__namespace_02wetric_8.returns: Never returns normally; always throws WetricUpstreamError, including when code is zero.
details: The WeTriC source is included with exit remapped to this function. run_wetric catches the exception as std::exception and reports execution_failed.
